methodology: Articles sourced from Virginia-specific RSS feeds and Google News RSS, filtered for AI/technology/workforce relevance, then assessed by Claude against the scenario framework. Each article is tagged with the region it most affects and the scenario it signals toward.

signals.title: Norfolk native brings free AI workshops to Hampton Roads to close the technology gap - WTKR
signals.signal_reading: Free AI workshops led by a local native in Hampton Roads signal grassroots capability-building through community networks, potentially distributing deep literacy beyond the NoVA/Richmond axis if sustained.

signals.title: Roanoke College launches WorkAI Lab to prepare leaders for new era of technology - Roanoke College
signals.signal_reading: Roanoke College's WorkAI Lab represents institutional investment in deep AI fluency outside metro centers, testing whether regional colleges can build distributed expertise or remain isolated pockets.

signals.title: Column: AI is reshaping Hampton Roads before our eyes - The Virginian-Pilot
signals.signal_reading: Hampton Roads observing AI reshaping the region suggests awareness without clear distribution mechanisms—signaling potential deepening in defense/maritime sectors while civilian applications remain concentrated.

signals.title: ‘Shaping our future’: Company powering AI data centers invests $50+ million in Henrico, adding 200 jobs - WWBT
signals.signal_reading: A $50M+ data center infrastructure investment in Henrico concentrates AI enabling infrastructure in Richmond Metro, creating jobs but reinforcing the capital-follows-capital pattern that widens geographic capability gaps.

signals.title: Virginia is developing a piecemeal data center moratorium. The potential impacts are complicated.
signals.signal_reading: Data center moratorium debates in historically underserved regions reveal communities lacking both infrastructure benefits and AI literacy to shape development terms—neither depth nor distribution is materializing where most needed.
